PullRequest.Title: Use report-question icon for sessions needing attention
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- replace the generic `report` icon with `report-question` when sessions need user attention
- keep the sessions model, agent sessions viewer, and experimental title-bar status widget consistent
- update focused tests and visual fixture descriptions

## Dependency

Depends on #340328 for the Codicon registration and `@vscode/codicons@0.0.46-44` package update.

## Validation

- `npm run eslint -- <8 changed files>`
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only`
- `./scripts/test.sh --grep 'report-question|matches sessions window state icons'` — 5 passing

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup and codicon asset registration/loading
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The codicon registry is initialized synchronously and the shared codicon font is loaded through the existing CSS asset path before glyphs can display; the PR adds one registry entry but does not add a new asset or request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the shared codicon font asset on a cold web load.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared font request per cold asset load, unchanged from before the PR; all codicons use the same resource.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same stylesheet loaded one shared codicon font; the dependency version changes the font contents but not boundary-call cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing font load gates glyph display, but the diff does not add a request or move it onto a new path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copy/read the codicon font during build packaging.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One source font copy in the existing build step, unchanged by the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior codicon package version supplied the same single font file to the same copy step.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Build-time only and not on an end-user interaction path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of registered codicons at startup; this change increases it by exactly one entry and one glyph in the existing font package.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Registration remains synchronous and linear during module initialization. The browser performs the same single shared font fetch/load as before, subject to its normal asset cache.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold startup loads the existing shared codicon font once; warm browser/resource caches reuse it. The new glyph does not use a separate cache key or trigger an additional font resource.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that startup registration grows by one constant-sized entry and font boundary cardinality is unchanged, based on the generated codicon library, package-only version bump, unchanged font CSS path, and unchanged build copy path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact byte delta between package font versions is not available from repository patches, but the diff establishes no additional font asset or boundary operation; one added glyph/registry object is not an actionable performance mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: only constant-size metadata/font growth is introduced, with no new request, repeated work, or meaningful startup scaling mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Sessions list, session header, and sessions picker rendering needs-attention status
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On row/header/picker rendering or a session status change, getStatusIcon selects a ThemeIcon and existing renderers create or reuse the same single status element. The glyph ID changes from report to report-question, while status evaluation, DOM cardinality, animation, and cache checks remain identical.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible session rows and status-change events. Effective cardinality remains one icon lookup and at most one status element per rendered session/header or picker item, exactly as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rendering remains synchronous on the UI thread and follows the existing list virtualization/event sequencing; the diff adds no tasks, promises, queues, or concurrent work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: SessionStatusIcon continues caching ThemeIcon.asCSSSelector and avoids rebuilding when the selector is unchanged. Changing the selected glyph only changes the cache-key value for NeedsInput, not cache lifetime or hit behavior after the first render.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from tracing SessionsListModelService.getStatusIcon into SessionStatusIcon and sessionsActions: the same object spread, CSS selector conversion, and one-element rendering occur before and after the PR.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual session counts and status-event frequency vary, but work per visible item/event and retained DOM are unchanged by the glyph substitution.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the changed status mapping substitutes an equivalent glyph without increasing synchronous UI work, allocation multiplicity, retained nodes, or boundary calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent sessions viewer row status rendering
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When an agent-session row is rendered or updated, getAgentSessionStatusIcon returns the selected ThemeIcon; the viewer compares its CSS-selector cache key and either recolors the existing element or replaces it with one span.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible agent-session rows and row update events. Effective cardinality remains one icon decision and no more than one active icon node per row.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing synchronous renderer updates remain unchanged; there is no added parallelism, scheduling, or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The per-renderer _currentCacheKey optimization is preserved. After the first NeedsInput render, repeated updates with the same glyph continue to reuse the existing element.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the viewer call path: only Codicon.report is replaced by Codicon.reportQuestion before the unchanged selector caching and DOM update logic.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of visible rows is product-dependent, but the per-row CPU, allocation, and DOM-node count are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: identical rendering and caching behavior with a different codepoint.

Scenarios.Scenario: Experimental agent title-bar status widget rendering attention indicators
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Widget rerenders compute existing session statistics and reconstruct status DOM; the changed lines pass report-question instead of report to renderIcon for the compact indicator and needs-input badge.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Widget rerender events and number of sessions scanned by the pre-existing statistics filters. The changed icon operation remains constant per render (at most the same attention indicator locations), independent of session count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All widget DOM rendering remains synchronous and sequenced by existing event listeners. The PR introduces no asynchronous work or concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is introduced or defeated. renderIcon creates the same one span for either glyph, and the shared font follows the existing cold/warm asset cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from both changed renderIcon call sites and surrounding render methods: only the ThemeIcon argument and local naming change; statistics scans, event listeners, node counts, and reset behavior are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Rerender frequency varies with session/configuration/theme events, but each changed site performs the same DOM allocation and class assignment as before.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no additional synchronous layout/render work, retained DOM, or event-driven repeated work is introduced.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 15 changed files and every diff page for the performance focus. The PR updates one codicon dependency/codepoint and substitutes that glyph across existing session status render paths and tests. Traced startup/font loading, sessions surfaces, agent-session rows, and the title-bar widget; boundary cardinality, concurrency, cache behavior, DOM cardinality, and asymptotic work remain unchanged. No valid performance finding or regression-fix learning signal was identified.
